compiled_state.description:
## Context
Project guidance currently describes `--force` and related override forms as human escape hatches, but it does not categorically prohibit agents from invoking them. Agents must stop and escalate to the user whenever an operation would require bypassing a configured gate or policy.

## Scope
Update only the canonical contributor/agent guidance in `AGENTS.md`. Preserve the command documentation needed for human operators while making the agent prohibition and escalation requirement unambiguous. No runtime enforcement or other documentation changes are part of this task.

## Plan
1. Add a concise, prominent rule near the existing claim and force-escape-hatch guidance.
2. Cover every force-style override command, including reason-bearing forms and force-close variants, without suggesting that an agent may use them after self-approval.
3. Require agents to stop, report the blocking condition, and ask the user to perform or explicitly direct the human-controlled next step.
4. Review the surrounding prose for consistency and run focused documentation checks plus the repository lint gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` explicitly prohibits agents from invoking any `--force`, `--force=<reason>`, or force-close override.
- [ ] The guidance requires escalation to the user when progress would depend on such an override.
- [ ] Existing human-operator escape-hatch documentation remains accurate and is clearly distinguished from agent behavior.
- [ ] No files outside `AGENTS.md` are intentionally modified.
- [ ] Relevant documentation checks and `make lint` pass.

file_impact.reason: Clarify the canonical agent policy for force-style overrides and user escalation.

compiled_state.title: Prohibit agent use of force overrides in project guidance
